claims.statement_id: Dalam Huainanzi, Feilian disebut sebagai makhluk yang dapat ditunggangi ke dunia roh tempat tidak ada yang binasa.
claims.quote: In the Huainanzi, Feilian is mentioned as a creature one can ride astride into the world of spirits where nothing perishes.

claims.statement: Eastern Han commentator Ying Shao defined Feilian as a sacred beast able to control the winds; the Jin commentator Jin Zhuo described it with a deer's body and a bird's head, horns, a snake's tail, and markings like a leopard's spots.
claims.statement_id: Komentator Han Timur Ying Shao mendefinisikan Feilian sebagai binatang suci yang mampu mengendalikan angin; komentator Jin Zhuo menyebutnya bertubuh rusa dengan kepala burung, bertanduk, berekor ular, dan bercorak seperti bintik macan tutul.
claims.quote: Eastern Han commentator Ying Shao defined Feilian as a sacred beast, able to control the winds. Jin dynasty commentator Jin Zhuo provided a more detailed description, saying Feilian had a deer's body with a bird's head, horns, and a snake's tail, with markings like a leopard's spots.

claims.statement: Modern English-language sources state Feilian is a winged dragon with the head of a deer and the tail of a snake; Hawkes states it is commonly depicted as a winged deer.
claims.statement_id: Sumber-sumber bahasa Inggris modern menyebut Feilian sebagai naga bersayap berkepala rusa dan berekor ular; Hawkes menyatakan ia umumnya digambarkan sebagai rusa bersayap.
claims.quote: Modern English language sources state Feilian is a winged dragon with the head of a deer and the tail of a snake. Hawkes states Feilian is commonly depicted as a winged deer,

claims.statement: In histories of the Zhou conquest of Shang, the Duke of Zhou pursued the Shang king Di Xin's minister Feilian to the seacoast and killed him there.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah penaklukan Zhou atas Shang, Adipati Zhou mengejar menteri Raja Di Xin dari Shang bernama Feilian ke pantai dan membunuhnya di sana.
claims.quote: the Duke of Zhou pursued Shang king Di Xin's minister Feilian to the seacoast and killed him there.

claims.statement: Qiongqi is a mythological creature in Chinese classics counted among the Four Perils.
claims.statement_id: Qiongqi adalah makhluk mitologis dalam teks klasik Tiongkok yang termasuk Empat Bahaya.
claims.quote: Qiongqi is a mythical creature mentioned in the Chinese classics. Along with Hundun, Taowu, and Taotie, it is one of the Four Perils.

claims.statement: Its name is interpreted as exhaustively strange.
claims.statement_id: Namanya diartikan sebagai sangat aneh.
claims.quote: Qiongqi (窮奇) literally means "exhaustively strange".

claims.statement: The Records of the Grand Historian portrays it as Shaohao's child acting disloyally and lying.
claims.statement_id: Catatan Sejarawan Agung menggambarkannya sebagai anak Shaohao yang tidak setia dan berbohong.
claims.quote: Qiongqi is mentioned in the Records of the Grand Historian as Shaohao's failed child, devoid of ability, who would act in bad faith, decry loyalty, and would speak only lies. Causing chaos across the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors period, he would eventually be banished by Emperor Shun of the Youyu clan to the far reaches of the region.

claims.statement: The Shanhaijing gives two conflicting descriptions of Qiongqi.
claims.statement_id: Shanhaijing memberikan dua gambaran Qiongqi yang saling bertentangan.
claims.quote: Qiongqi is given two conflicting descriptions in the Classic of Mountains and Seas.

claims.statement: This text says that on Mount Gui there lives a beast shaped like an ox with hedgehog-like bristles, named Qiongqi, whose cry is like a barking dog, and that it "eats people".
claims.statement_id: Teks ini menyebut di Gunung Gui ada seekor binatang berbentuk seperti sapi berbulu seperti landak, bernama Qiongqi, bersuara seperti anjing menggonggong, dan "memakan orang".
claims.quote: 曰邽〈音圭〉山。其上有獸焉，其狀如牛，猬毛，名曰窮奇，音如獆狗，是食人

claims.statement: This text says Qiongqi is shaped like a winged tiger, eats people starting from the head, the people it eats have disheveled hair, and it lives north of Taoquan; another version says it starts from the feet.
claims.statement_id: Teks ini menyebut Qiongqi berbentuk seperti harimau bersayap, memakan orang mulai dari kepala dan mangsanya berambut terurai, tinggal di sebelah utara Taoquan; versi lain menyebut ia mulai dari kaki.
claims.quote: 窮奇狀如虎，有翼，食人從首始，所食被髮，在蜪犬北。一曰從足。

claims.statement: The Book of Gods and Strange Things embellishes the second description, adding that Qiongqi understands human speech; if it hears people fighting it eats the one in the right, if it hears one who is loyal and trustworthy it eats their nose, and if it hears someone wicked it kills a beast to feed them.
claims.statement_id: Book of Gods and Strange Things memperluas gambaran kedua dengan menambahkan bahwa Qiongqi memahami bahasa manusia; bila mendengar orang bertengkar ia memakan pihak yang benar, bila mendengar orang setia dan dapat dipercaya ia memakan hidungnya, dan bila mendengar orang jahat ia membunuh binatang untuk diberikan kepadanya.
claims.quote: The second account is embellished in the Book of Gods and Strange Things, which, in addition to the above description, also claims that Qiongqi understands human speech. ... If it hears people fighting, it will eat the one in the right, and if it hears one who is loyal and trustworthy, it will eat their nose. If it hears someone wicked, it will kill a beast to feed them.

claims.statement: The Zuo Zhuan speaks to similar effect but goes further, stating that the Qiongqi elevated lies, spread false accusations, and would stay quiet before slandering people.
claims.statement_id: Zuo Zhuan menyatakan hal serupa tetapi lebih jauh: Qiongqi menjunjung dusta, menyebarkan tuduhan palsu, dan diam sebelum memfitnah orang.
claims.quote: The Zuo Zhuan speaks to similar effect, but goes further, stating that the Qiongqi elevated lies, spread false accusations, and would stay quiet before slandering people.

claims.statement: In the biographies it is also written that Qiongqi resides in a place called Yunmeng in the State of Chu.
claims.statement_id: Dalam biografi-biografi itu juga ditulis bahwa Qiongqi tinggal di tempat bernama Yunmeng di Negara Chu.
claims.quote: In the biographies, he also writes that it resides in a place called Yunmeng (雲夢 ) in the State of Chu.

claims.statement: Qiongqi is featured in the Shin Megami Tensei franchise, particularly the Devil Children games, as a recruitable demon, using the description from the Classic of the Northern Seas' Inner Realm in the Classic of Mountains and Seas.
claims.statement_id: Qiongqi tampil dalam waralaba Shin Megami Tensei, terutama gim Devil Children, sebagai iblis yang dapat direkrut, dengan memakai penggambaran dari Hainei beijing dalam Classic of Mountains and Seas.
claims.quote: Qiongqi is featured in the Shin Megami Tensei franchise, particularly the Devil Children games, as a recruitable demon, using the description from the Classic of the Northern Seas' Inner Realm (海內北經 ) of the Classic of Mountains and Seas.

claims.statement: Shenlong is a Chinese mythological spirit dragon governing rain and tempests.
claims.statement_id: Shenlong adalah naga roh dalam mitologi Tiongkok yang menguasai hujan dan badai.
claims.quote: Shenlong (simplified Chinese: 神龙; traditional Chinese: 神龍; pinyin: shén lóng, literally "god dragon" or "divine dragon", Japanese: 神龍, shinryū) is the spirit dragon from Chinese mythology who is the dragon god of the tempest and also a master of rain.

claims.statement: Shenlong is described as a god of tempest and master of rain.
claims.statement_id: Shenlong disebut dewa badai dan penguasa hujan.
claims.quote: is the spirit dragon from Chinese mythology who is the dragon god of the tempest and also a master of rain.

claims.statement: This classical text, the Guanzi, states that the dragon (龍) is born in water and roams wearing five colors, hence it is "shen" (divine); it can shrink to a silkworm, grow so large it hides beneath heaven, rise above the clouds or descend into deep springs, and its changes are not bound to day or time.
claims.statement_id: Teks klasik Guanzi ini menyatakan naga (龍) lahir di air dan mengembara dengan lima warna sehingga disebut "shen" (ilahi); ia dapat mengecil menjadi seperti ulat sutra, membesar hingga bersembunyi di bawah langit, naik melampaui awan, atau turun ke mata air dalam, dan perubahannya tak terikat hari maupun waktu.
claims.quote: 龍生於水，被五色而游，故神。欲小則化如蠶蠋，欲大則藏於天下，欲上則凌於雲氣，欲下則入於深泉。變化無日，上下無時，謂之神。

claims.statement: The spiritual dragon is azure-scaled and governs the storms, clouds and rain on which all agricultural life depends.
claims.statement_id: Naga roh ini bersisik biru langit dan menguasai badai, awan, dan hujan yang menjadi sandaran seluruh kehidupan pertanian.
claims.quote: The spiritual dragon is azure-scaled and governs the storms, clouds, and rain on which all agricultural life depends.

claims.statement: In the classical dictionary text Shuowen Jiezi, the dragon (龍) is the chief of scaly creatures; it can be hidden or bright, small or huge, short or long, rising to heaven at the spring equinox and diving into the deep at the autumn equinox.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks kamus klasik Shuowen Jiezi, naga (龍) adalah yang tertua di antara makhluk bersisik; ia dapat tersembunyi atau terang, kecil atau besar, pendek atau panjang, naik ke langit pada ekuinoks musim semi dan menyelam ke samudra pada ekuinoks musim gugur.
claims.quote: 龍（ ）：鱗蟲之長。能幽，能明，能細，能巨，能短，能長；春分而登天，秋分而潛淵。

claims.statement: Li Shizhen's Bencao Gangmu says the dragon has a "Boshan", also called "chimu", on its head, without which it cannot ascend to heaven, and that its breath forms clouds and it can change into water or fire.
claims.statement_id: Bencao Gangmu karya Li Shizhen menyebut naga memiliki "Boshan" atau "chimu" di kepalanya, yang tanpanya naga tidak dapat naik ke langit, dan bahwa napasnya membentuk awan serta dapat mengubah diri menjadi air atau api.
claims.quote: 頭上有博山，又名尺木，龍無尺木不能升天。呵氣成雲，既能變水，又能變火。

claims.statement: According to the Bencao Gangmu, the dragon's nature is rough and fierce; it loves fine jade and kongqing and is fond of swallow meat, and fears iron, wangcao grass, centipedes, chinaberry leaves and five-colored silk.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Bencao Gangmu, naga bersifat kasar dan garang, menyukai batu giok indah dan kongqing serta daging burung layang-layang, dan takut pada besi, rumput wangcao, kelabang, daun chinaberry, dan benang lima warna.
claims.quote: 龍性粗猛，而愛美玉、空青，喜嗜燕肉，畏鐵及菵草、蜈蚣、楝葉、五色絲。

claims.statement: Shōjō is the Japanese reading of the Chinese mythical ape name xing-xing.
claims.statement_id: Shōjō adalah bacaan Jepang dari nama kera mitologis Tiongkok xing-xing.
claims.quote: A shōjō (猩々 or 猩猩) is the Japanese reading of Chinese xing-xing (猩猩) or its older form sheng sheng (狌狌, translated as "live-lively"), which is a mythical ape, though it has been tentatively identified as an (unknown) orangutan species.

claims.statement: The sea-spirit portrayal occurs in the Noh play Shōjō and does not by itself establish native Japanese tradition.
claims.statement_id: Penggambaran sebagai roh laut muncul dalam lakon Noh Shōjō dan tidak otomatis membuktikan tradisi asli Jepang.
claims.quote: Some commentators have regarded the shōjō sea spirit with a red face and hair and a fondness for alcohol as part of native Japanese folklore. However, shōjō as sea-dwelling spirit was a fictional setting in the Noh play Shōjō, a possible embellishment of the Shan Hai Jing ("Classic of Mountains and Seas") stating this orangutan could be found on a particular seaside mountain.

claims.statement: Shōjō also denotes orangutans and may describe people fond of alcohol.
claims.statement_id: Istilah shōjō juga berarti orangutan dan dapat menyebut peminum alkohol.
claims.quote: The Chinese characters are also a Japanese (and Chinese) word for orangutan, and can also be used in Japanese to refer to someone who is particularly fond of alcohol.

claims.statement: Shōjō names a Noh mask and a Kabuki stage-makeup type.
claims.statement_id: Nama shōjō digunakan untuk topeng Noh dan jenis rias panggung Kabuki.
claims.quote: A Noh mask called the shōjō exists (cf. §Noh); also, in Kabuki, a type of stage makeup (kumadori) is called the shōjō.

claims.statement: Japanese tale portrayals give it a red face and hair and a fondness for alcohol.
claims.statement_id: Penggambaran cerita Jepang memberikan wajah serta rambut merah dan kegemaran alkohol.
claims.quote: The shōjō has been represented as a sea spirit with a red face and hair and a fondness for alcohol as part of Japanese folktale tradition.

claims.statement: This classical text, the Shanhaijing, mentions a beast shaped like a yu (a monkey-like animal) with white ears that goes bent over but runs like a person, named 狌狌 (shengsheng), and eating it makes one good at running.
claims.statement_id: Teks klasik Shanhaijing ini menyebut seekor binatang berbentuk seperti yu (sejenis monyet) berkuping putih, berjalan merunduk tetapi berlari seperti manusia, bernama 狌狌 (shengsheng), dan yang memakannya menjadi pandai berlari.
claims.quote: 有獸焉，其狀如禺〈禺似獼猴而大赤目，長者不了此物名禺。作牛字圖，亦做牛形或作猴，皆失之也。禺字音遇，〉而白耳，伏行人走，其名曰狌狌〈狌狌，禺獸。狀如猿，伏行交足亦此類也。見《京房易》〉，食之善走。

claims.statement: This classical text, the Shanhaijing, puts the forest 氾林, three hundred li square, east of the 狌狌; the 狌狌 know the names of people, are beasts like pigs but with human faces, and are located west of Shun's burial place.
claims.statement_id: Teks klasik Shanhaijing ini menyebut hutan 氾林 seluas tiga ratus li di sebelah timur 狌狌; 狌狌 mengetahui nama manusia, berwujud binatang seperti babi tetapi berwajah manusia, di sebelah barat makam Shun.
claims.quote: 氾林方三百里，在狌狌東。 狌狌知人名，其為獸如豕而人面，在舜葬西。

claims.statement: The article's passage on the Bencao Gangmu says these creatures are lured by leaving straw sandals and liquor by the roadside; they examine the goods and go away at first, but return to try on the sandals and drink the wine, at which point they can be captured.
claims.statement_id: Bagian artikel tentang Bencao Gangmu menyebut bahwa makhluk ini dipikat dengan meninggalkan sandal jerami dan arak di tepi jalan; mereka mula-mula memeriksa lalu pergi, tetapi kembali mencoba sandal dan meminum arak, saat itulah mereka dapat ditangkap.
claims.quote: The Bencao Gangmu describes it as resembling a dog or rhesus macaque ... It cites Ruan Qian ... They would leave straw sandals and liquor by the roadside to lure them; the creatures examine these goods but go away at first, but they return to try on the sandals and drink the wine, at which point they can be captured.

claims.statement: In the Noh play Shōjō, the shōjō disguised as a human buys sake in large quantity yet his face never flushes; he then appears in his true form, drinks, dances ecstatically and rewards the seller by making his sake vat perpetually refill itself.
claims.statement_id: Dalam lakon Noh Shōjō, tokoh shōjō yang menyamar sebagai manusia membeli sake dalam jumlah besar tetapi wajahnya tidak memerah; ia kemudian tampil dalam wujud aslinya, minum, menari riang, dan sebagai imbalan membuat tong sake sang penjual terisi kembali terus-menerus.
claims.quote: The Kyōgen-influenced Noh play shōjō is set in Ancient China ... The protagonist (shite) shōjō disguised as a human buys from him in large quantity, but his face never becomes flushed despite the heavy drinking. ... The shōjō appears in its true form, drinks the sake, getting drunk and dancing ecstatically, then rewarding the sake seller by making his sake vat perpetually refill itself.

claims.statement: The Shōjō doll was a hariko (papier-mâché) like the daruma, considered a lucky item (engimono) placed on the hearth, and was supposed to contract the pox in place of the family.
claims.statement_id: Boneka Shōjō berupa hariko (kertas mâché) seperti daruma dan dianggap benda pembawa keberuntungan (engimono) yang diletakkan di tungku, dan dianggap menanggung cacar sebagai pengganti keluarga.
claims.quote: The Shōjō doll was a hariko (papier-mâché) like the daruma ... It was considered a lucky item (engimono), placed on the hearth (kamado), and was supposed to contract the pox in place of the family.

claims.statement: The shōjō has sometimes been misconceived as purely native Japanese folklore and superstition, particularly by commentators of the netsuke craft art, since it is a popular subject for these carvings.
claims.statement_id: Shōjō kadang disalahpahami sebagai cerita rakyat asli Jepang murni, terutama oleh pengulas seni netsuke, karena shōjō adalah subjek populer pada ukiran itu.
claims.quote: It has sometimes been misconceived as purely native Japanese folklore and superstition, particularly by commentators of the netsuke craft art, since the shōjō is a popular subject for these carvings.

claims.statement: Tiangou is a Chinese legendary creature resembling a black dog or meteor.
claims.statement_id: Tiangou adalah makhluk legenda Tiongkok berupa anjing hitam atau meteor.
claims.quote: is a legendary creature from China. The tiangou resembles a black dog or meteor, and is thought to eat the Sun or Moon during an eclipse.

claims.statement: This creature is believed to eat the sun or moon during an eclipse.
claims.statement_id: Makhluk ini dipercaya memakan matahari atau bulan saat gerhana.
claims.quote: is a legendary creature from China. The tiangou resembles a black dog or meteor, and is thought to eat the Sun or Moon during an eclipse.

claims.statement: In a benevolent variant, it resembles a white-headed fox offering protection.
claims.statement_id: Dalam varian baik, ia menyerupai rubah berkepala putih yang memberikan perlindungan.
claims.quote: As a good spirit, it has the appearance of a white-headed fox. It brings peace and tranquility, and gives protection from all sorts of troubles and robbers. It is referred to by astrologers as a constellation guardian of welfare. This asterism consists of seven stars. In ancient Chinese astronomy, Tiangou ('Heavenly Dog') referred to an asterism located in the region of Argo Navis.

claims.statement: The adverse variant portrays it as a black dog that eats the moon.
claims.statement_id: Varian buruk menggambarkannya sebagai anjing hitam pemakan bulan.
claims.quote: As a bad spirit, it is a black dog that eats the Moon. According to the legends, as an interpretation of a lunar eclipse, after Houyi shot down the nine Suns in the sky, he was awarded with an immortality-granting pill by the Queen Mother of the West. Before he could eat it, his wife Chang'e consumed the elixir of immortality. Chang'e felt her body getting lighter and flew away.

claims.statement: One tale describes the Queen Mother of the West capturing the dog and making it heaven's gatekeeper.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kisah menyebut Ibu Suri dari Barat menangkap anjing dan menjadikannya penjaga gerbang langit.
claims.quote: After being informed of this, the Queen Mother of the West captured the dog. Surprised to see that the dog was actually Hou Yi's, she assigned him to guard the gates of heavens and bestowed upon him the title of Tiangou. Tiangou spat the Moon and Chang'e back out, and Chang'e continued living on the Moon.

claims.statement: Zhang Xian is portrayed as its adversary using a bow and arrows.
claims.statement_id: Zhang Xian digambarkan sebagai lawannya yang menggunakan busur dan panah.
claims.quote: Zhang Xian (Chinese: 張仙; pinyin: Zhāng Xiān) is the enemy of the tiangou. It is said that he protects his children from the dog god with his bow and arrows. He is often depicted aiming at the sky, waiting for the beast to appear.

claims.statement: This classical text, the Shanhaijing, says that on Mount Yin there is a beast shaped like a 狸 (a wildcat-like small animal) with a white head, named Tiangou ("heavenly dog"), whose cry sounds like "liuliu", and which can be used to ward off calamity.
claims.statement_id: Teks klasik Shanhaijing ini menyebut di Gunung Yin ada binatang berbentuk seperti 狸 (binatang kecil mirip kucing liar) berkepala putih, bernama Tiangou ("anjing langit"), bersuara seperti "liuliu", dan dapat dipakai untuk menangkal bencana.
claims.quote: 曰陰山。濁浴之水出焉，而南流注于蕃澤，其中多文貝〈餘泉蚳之𩔖也，見爾雅。〉。有獸焉，其狀如狸〈或作豹。〉而白首，名曰天狗，其音如榴榴〈或作猫猫。〉，可以禦凶。

claims.statement: This historical text, the Shiji, describes the 天狗 as a heavenly sign shaped like a great shooting star, with sound, whose lower part settles on the ground resembling a dog; where it falls it looks like blazing fire reaching heaven, and it portends armies broken and generals killed for a thousand li.
claims.statement_id: Teks sejarah Shiji ini menyebut 天狗 sebagai tanda langit berbentuk seperti bintang jatuh besar, bersuara, yang bagian bawahnya jatuh ke bumi menyerupai anjing; tempat jatuhnya tampak seperti api yang menjulang, dan ia mengisyaratkan pasukan hancur serta jenderal terbunuh sejauh seribu li.
claims.quote: 天狗，狀如大奔星，〈【集解】孟康曰：「星有尾，旁有短彗，下有如狗形者，亦太白之精。」〉有聲，其下止地，類狗。所墮及，望之如火光炎炎〈【索隱】艷音也。〉衝天。其下圜如數頃田處，上兌者則有黃色，千里破軍殺將。

claims.statement: Zhang Xian is the god of birth and the protector of male children; many sought him to give them male offspring and to protect their living sons.
claims.statement_id: Zhang Xian adalah dewa kelahiran dan pelindung anak laki-laki; banyak orang memintanya memberi keturunan laki-laki dan melindungi putra-putra mereka yang hidup.
claims.quote: Zhang Xian (Chinese: 張仙; pinyin: Zhāng Xiān) is the enemy of the tiangou. ... He is the god of birth and the protector of male children. Many sought for him to give them male offspring and to protect their living sons.

claims.statement: In the legend, a black dog Hou Yi was rearing went into Chang'e's room and licked the remains of the immortality pill, chased after her getting bigger and bigger, and ate the Moon along with Chang'e.
claims.statement_id: Dalam legenda, seekor anjing hitam milik Hou Yi menjilat sisa pil keabadian di kamar Chang'e, mengejarnya sambil terus membesar, lalu memakan Bulan bersama Chang'e.
claims.quote: Seeing this, a black dog that Hou Yi was rearing went inside her room and licked the remains of the pill. He then chased after Chang'e, getting bigger and bigger. Chang'e, terrified, hid on the Moon. The black dog then ate the Moon, along with Chang'e.

claims.statement: In the tale, Tiangou spat the Moon and Chang'e back out, and Chang'e continued living on the Moon.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kisah itu, Tiangou memuntahkan kembali Bulan dan Chang'e, dan Chang'e terus hidup di Bulan.
claims.quote: Tiangou spat the Moon and Chang'e back out, and Chang'e continued living on the Moon.

claims.statement: Xingtian is a Chinese deity who opposes the supreme divinity even after decapitation.
claims.statement_id: Xingtian adalah dewa Tiongkok yang melawan penguasa ilahi bahkan setelah dipenggal.
claims.quote: Xingtian (Chinese: 刑天; pinyin: Xíngtiān; lit. 'Punishing Heaven', also Hsing T'ien) is a Chinese deity who fights against the Supreme Divinity, not giving up even after he was decapitated. Losing the fight for supremacy, he was beheaded and his head buried in Changyang Mountain.

claims.statement: His head is buried at Changyang Mountain after defeat in a struggle for supremacy.
claims.statement_id: Kepalanya dikubur di Gunung Changyang setelah kalah memperebutkan kekuasaan.
claims.quote: Xingtian (Chinese: 刑天; pinyin: Xíngtiān; lit. 'Punishing Heaven', also Hsing T'ien) is a Chinese deity who fights against the Supreme Divinity, not giving up even after he was decapitated. Losing the fight for supremacy, he was beheaded and his head buried in Changyang Mountain.

claims.statement: One account calls Xingtian an official of Yandi continuing resistance against Huangdi.
claims.statement_id: Versi kisah menyebut Xingtian sebagai pejabat Yandi yang melanjutkan perlawanan kepada Huangdi.
claims.quote: Xingtian was an official under Yandi. Yandi fought against Huangdi for the position of supreme god, but he lost the conflict. Xingtian still continued the fight after Yandi's defeat, but was defeated and decapitated by Huangdi. Eventually, he regenerated himself and continued his defiance, which was expressed by a martial dance.

claims.statement: Chapter seven of the Shanhaijing records Xingtian's resistance.
claims.statement_id: Bab ketujuh Shanhaijing mencatat perlawanan Xingtian.
claims.quote: Xingtian appears in chapter 7 of the Classic of Mountains and Seas, which states that he fought and lost against the supreme god to become the supreme divinity. The god decapitated Xingtian and buried his head on Changyang Mountain. However, Xingtian persevered, using his nipples as his eyes, using his navel as his mouth, and brandishing his shield and axe.

claims.statement: He uses his nipples as eyes and navel as mouth while dancing with axe and shield.
claims.statement_id: Ia memakai puting sebagai mata dan pusar sebagai mulut sambil menari dengan kapak dan perisai.
claims.quote:
Xingtian and the Supreme God Di came to this place and struggled against each other for ultimate power. The Supreme God cut off Xingtian's head
and buried him at Eternally Auspicious Mountain. Xiangtian's nipples then transformed into eyes, and his navel became a mouth. He performs a dance with an axe and shield."

claims.statement: Luo Mi's Lushi links him to music for farming activities.
claims.statement_id: Lushi karya Luo Mi menghubungkannya dengan musik untuk kegiatan pertanian.
claims.quote: In Luo Mi's Lushi from the Southern Song period, Xingtian is described as a minister of the Yan Emperor, who composed music for farmers for plowing and harvesting.

claims.statement: This classical text says Xingtian (written 刑天, with a variant 形天) contended with the Di for divinity; the Di cut off his head and buried it on Mount Changyang, and he then used his nipples as eyes and his navel as a mouth, wielding shield and axe in dance.
claims.statement_id: Teks klasik ini menyebut Xingtian (tertulis 刑天, dengan varian 形天) berebut keilahian dengan sang Di; Di memenggal kepalanya dan menguburnya di Gunung Changyang, lalu ia menjadikan puting sebagai mata dan pusar sebagai mulut, memegang perisai dan kapak untuk menari.
claims.quote: 刑一作「形」天與帝 爭神一作「至此爭神」，帝斷其首，葬之常羊之山，乃以乳為目，以臍為口，操干戚以舞。

claims.statement: In this poem the poet writes that Jingwei holds twigs in her bill to fill the deep-blue sea, and Xingtian dances with shield and axe, his fierce will ever present; after blending with things no anxieties remain, and after transforming no regrets.
claims.statement_id: Dalam puisi ini, penyair menulis bahwa Jingwei menggigit ranting kecil untuk mengisi laut biru, dan Xingtian menari dengan perisai dan kapak, tekad garangnya selalu ada; setelah berbaur dengan segala hal tak ada lagi kecemasan, dan setelah berubah tak ada lagi penyesalan.
claims.quote: 精衛銜微木，將以填滄海； 刑天舞干戚，猛志故常在。 同物既無慮，化去不復悔。

claims.statement: The scholar Guo Pu celebrated Xingtian's defiant spirit in an encomium, mentioning the similarity between Xingtian and the corpse of Geng of the Xia since both were characters who regenerated and continued their resistance.
claims.statement_id: Sarjana Guo Pu memuji semangat pembangkangan Xingtian dalam sebuah pujian, dan menyebut kemiripan Xingtian dengan jasad Geng dari Xia karena keduanya tokoh yang pulih kembali dan terus melawan.
claims.quote: The scholar Guo Pu celebrated Xingtian's defiant spirit in an encomium. ... He mentions the similarity between Xingtian and the corpse of Geng of the Xia, since they were both characters who regenerated and continued their resistance.

claims.statement: In the Huainanzi, Xingtian is called the corpse of Xingcan (形殘之尸).
claims.statement_id: Dalam Huainanzi, Xingtian disebut jasad Xingcan (形殘之尸).
claims.quote: In the Huainanzi, Xingtian is called the corpse of Xingcan

claims.statement: Xingtian symbolizes the indomitable spirit which maintains the will to resist no matter what tribulations one may undergo or what troubles one may encounter.
claims.statement_id: Xingtian melambangkan semangat tak terkalahkan yang mempertahankan tekad melawan apa pun cobaan atau masalah yang dihadapi seseorang.
claims.quote: Xingtian symbolizes the indomitable spirit which maintains the will to resist no matter what tribulations one may undergo or what troubles one may encounter.

claims.statement: Bashe is a python-like giant serpent in Chinese mythology that eats elephants.
claims.statement_id: Bashe adalah ular raksasa mitologi Tiongkok yang menyerupai piton dan memakan gajah.
claims.quote: Bashe (Chinese: 巴蛇; pinyin: bā-shé; Wade–Giles: pa-she) was a python-like Chinese mythological giant snake that ate elephants.

claims.statement: Its name combines elements for an elephant-eating snake and a serpent.
claims.statement_id: Namanya menggabungkan unsur ular pemakan gajah dan ular.
claims.quote: The term bashe compounds ba 巴 "elephant-eating snake" and she 蛇 "snake; serpent".

claims.statement: Bashe has also been used as an alternative name for pythons.
claims.statement_id: Nama Bashe juga pernah digunakan sebagai nama alternatif piton.
claims.quote: Bashe not only names this mythical giant reptile but is also a variant Chinese name for the South Asian ran 蚺 or mang 蟒 "python" (and South American "boa constrictor" or African "mamba").

claims.statement: Early Bashe references occur in the Chu Ci and Shanhaijing.
claims.statement_id: Rujukan awal Bashe ditemukan dalam Chu Ci dan Shanhaijing.
claims.quote: The earliest references to the legendary bashe 巴蛇 are in the Chuci and Shanhaijing, two Chinese classic texts containing Warring States period (475 BCE – 221 BCE) materials compiled during the Han dynasty (206 BCE – 220 CE).

claims.statement: This classical text says the 巴蛇 eats elephants and disgorges the bones after three years; a gentleman who takes it has no illness of heart or belly; the snake is green-blue, yellow, red or black, with another account of a black snake with a green-blue head, located west of the rhinoceros.
claims.statement_id: Teks klasik ini menyebut 巴蛇 memakan gajah dan mengeluarkan tulangnya setelah tiga tahun; "junzi" yang meminumnya tak terkena penyakit jantung dan perut; ular itu berwarna hijau-biru, kuning, merah, atau hitam, dan ada yang menyebut ular hitam berkepala hijau-biru, di sebelah barat badak.
claims.quote: 巴蛇食象，三歲而出其骨，君子服之，無心腹之疾。其為蛇青黃赤黑。一曰黑蛇青首，在犀牛西。

claims.statement: Guo Pu's commentary on the Shanhaijing compares the ba snake with the southern ran 蚺 (python), which after eating a large animal can wind around a tree trunk and expel the bones from between its scales, and notes they could grow up to 100 xun in length.
claims.statement_id: Komentar Guo Pu atas Shanhaijing membandingkan ular ba dengan ran 蚺 (piton) selatan, yang setelah memakan hewan besar dapat melilit batang pohon dan mengeluarkan tulangnya dari sela sisiknya, dan mencatat panjangnya dapat mencapai 100 xun.
claims.quote: The Shanhaijing commentary by Guo Pu (276–324 CE) compares the ba snake with the southern ran 蚺 "python", which after eating a large animal can wind around a tree trunk and expel the bones from between its scales and notes they could grow up to a length of 100 xun

claims.statement: In literary usage, bashe is found in the four-character idiom bashetunxiang (巴蛇吞象, "ba-snake gulping down an elephant"), meaning inordinately greedy and extremely insatiable.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penggunaan sastra, bashe ditemukan dalam peribahasa empat aksara bashetunxiang (巴蛇吞象, "ular ba menelan gajah") yang berarti sangat serakah dan tak pernah puas.
claims.quote: In literary usage, bashe is found in the four-character idiom bashetunxiang 巴蛇吞象 (lit. "ba-snake gulping down an elephant") meaning "inordinately greedy; extremely insatiable".

claims.statement: The folklore scholar Wolfram Eberhard links bashe with the legendary archer Houyi, who descended from heaven to destroy evildoers; one of Houyi's victims was a monstrous serpent in Lake Dongting.
claims.statement_id: Pakar cerita rakyat Wolfram Eberhard mengaitkan bashe dengan pemanah legendaris Houyi yang turun dari langit untuk menumpas pelaku kejahatan; salah satu korban Houyi adalah ular raksasa di Danau Dongting.
claims.quote: The Chinese folklore scholar Wolfram Eberhard links bashe with the legendary archer Houyi 后翌 who descended from heaven to destroy evildoers. One of Houyi's victims was a monstrous serpent in Lake Dongting,

claims.statement: Kui is a name with multiple senses in Chinese mythology, including a one-legged mountain being.
claims.statement_id: Kui adalah nama bermakna majemuk dalam mitologi Tiongkok, termasuk makhluk gunung berkaki satu.
claims.quote: Kui (Chinese: 夔; pinyin:  kuí; Wade–Giles: k'uei) is a polysemous figure in ancient Chinese mythology. Classic texts use this name for the legendary musician Kui who invented music and dancing; for the one-legged mountain demon or rain-god Kui variously said to resemble a Chinese dragon, a drum, or a monkey with a human face; and for the Kuiniu wild yak or buffalo.

claims.statement: The same name also denotes a legendary musician credited with music and dance.
claims.statement_id: Nama yang sama juga digunakan untuk musisi legenda pencipta musik dan tarian.
claims.quote: Kui (Chinese: 夔; pinyin:  kuí; Wade–Giles: k'uei) is a polysemous figure in ancient Chinese mythology. Classic texts use this name for the legendary musician Kui who invented music and dancing; for the one-legged mountain demon or rain-god Kui variously said to resemble a Chinese dragon, a drum, or a monkey with a human face; and for the Kuiniu wild yak or buffalo.

claims.statement: Kuilong and kuiwen motifs appear on Zhou bronzes.
claims.statement_id: Motif kuilong dan kuiwen muncul pada perunggu zaman Zhou.
claims.quote: While Kui (夔) originally named a mythic being, Modern Standard Chinese uses it in several other expressions. The reduplication kuíkuí (夔夔) means "awe-struck; fearful; grave" (see the Shujing below). The compounds kuílóng (夔龍) (with "dragon") and kuíwén (夔紋) (with "pattern; design") name common motifs on Zhou dynasty Chinese bronzes.

claims.statement: Translating Kui as walrus is explained as a dictionary error rather than its Chinese meaning.
claims.statement_id: Penerjemahan Kui sebagai walrus dijelaskan sebagai kekeliruan kamus, bukan makna Tiongkok aslinya.
claims.quote: Translating kuí (夔) as "walrus" exemplifies a ghost word. The Unihan Database lists the definition as "one-legged monster; walrus". However, Chinese kui does not mean "walrus" (海象; hǎixiàng; 'sea elephant'), and this ghost first appeared in early Chinese-English dictionaries by Robert Henry Mathews and Herbert Giles.

claims.statement: The text says that on the mountain called Liubo (流波山) in the East Sea there is a beast named Kui, shaped like an ox, with a blue-green body, no horns, and one foot.
claims.statement_id: Teks ini menyebut bahwa di gunung bernama Liubo (流波山) di tengah Laut Timur ada seekor binatang bernama Kui, berbentuk seperti lembu, bertubuh biru kehijauan, tanpa tanduk, dan berkaki satu.
claims.quote: 東海中有流波山，入海七千里。其上有獸，狀如牛，蒼身而無角，一足，出入水則必風雨，其光如日月，其聲如雷，其名曰夔。

claims.statement: The text states that whenever the beast goes into or out of the water there is wind and rain, its glare is like the sun and moon, and its voice is like thunder.
claims.statement_id: Teks ini menyatakan bahwa setiap kali binatang itu keluar masuk air pasti ada angin dan hujan, sinarnya seperti matahari dan bulan, dan suaranya seperti guntur.
claims.quote: 其上有獸，狀如牛，蒼身而無角，一足，出入水則必風雨，其光如日月，其聲如雷，其名曰夔。

claims.statement: The text states that the Yellow Emperor obtained it, made its hide into a drum and struck it with a bone of the thunder beast; the sound was heard for five hundred li and awed all under heaven.
claims.statement_id: Teks ini menyatakan bahwa Kaisar Kuning (Huangdi) memperolehnya, membuat kulitnya menjadi gendang dan memukulnya dengan tulang binatang guntur; bunyinya terdengar sejauh lima ratus li dan membuat gentar seisi dunia.
claims.quote: 其名曰夔。黃帝得之，以其皮為鼓，橛以雷獸之骨，聲聞五百里，以威天下。

claims.statement: An ancient commentary quoted in the article says some hold that the khwei have one leg, and that they have a human face, an ape-like body, and can speak.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah komentar kuno yang dikutip artikel ini menyebut sebagian orang mengatakan khwei berkaki satu, dan bahwa mereka berwajah manusia, bertubuh seperti kera, dan dapat berbicara.
claims.quote: Some say that the khwei have one leg. ... They exist in Fu-yang (about the present Hang-cheu), have a human countenance and an ape-like body, and can speak.

claims.statement: A text quoted in the article describes another mountain power shaped like a drum, red, and one-footed, named Hui, which the article notes as a variant name of Kui.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah teks yang dikutip artikel ini menyebut satu lagi kekuatan gunung berbentuk gendang, berwarna merah, dan berkaki satu, bernama Hui, yang dalam artikel dicatat sebagai nama lain Kui.
claims.quote: There is another mountain power, this one in the shape of a drum, colored red, and also with only one foot. Its name is Hui.

claims.statement: The article explains that Confucianist revisionism reads the phrase not as "Kui [had] one foot" but as "one person like Kui was enough".
claims.statement_id: Artikel ini menjelaskan bahwa revisionisme Konfusianis membaca ungkapan itu bukan sebagai "Kui [berkaki] satu" melainkan "satu orang seperti Kui sudah cukup".
claims.quote: as "Kui [had] one foot", Confucianist revisionism construes it as "Kui, one [person like him] was enough."

claims.statement: A passage quoted in the article states that apparitions between trees and rocks are called khwei and wang-liang, while those in the water are called lung, or dragons.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah kutipan dalam artikel ini menyatakan bahwa penampakan di antara pohon dan batu disebut khwei dan wang-liang, sedangkan yang di dalam air disebut lung (naga).
claims.quote: apparitions between trees and rocks are called khwei and wang-liang, while those in the water are lung or dragons

claims.statement: Longma is a winged horse bearing dragon scales in Chinese mythology.
claims.statement_id: Longma adalah kuda bersayap dengan sisik naga dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: The longma is a fabled winged horse with dragon scales in Chinese mythology. Seeing a longma was an omen of a legendary sage-ruler, particularly one of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors.

claims.statement: Its appearance is regarded as an omen of a sage ruler.
claims.statement_id: Kemunculannya dipandang sebagai pertanda seorang penguasa bijak.
claims.quote: The longma is a fabled winged horse with dragon scales in Chinese mythology. Seeing a longma was an omen of a legendary sage-ruler, particularly one of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors.

claims.statement: Its name joins long for dragon with ma for horse.
claims.statement_id: Namanya menggabungkan kata long untuk naga dan ma untuk kuda.
claims.quote: The Chinese word longma combines long (龍; "dragon") and ma (馬). Compare hema (河馬; 'river horse'; "hippopotamus") and haima (海馬; 'sea horse'; "seahorse"). In addition to naming the mythic creature, longma (龍馬; "dragon horse") can refer to an eminent person, such as in the four-character idiom 龍馬精神; longma jingshen; "vigorous spirit in old age".

claims.statement: The Zhouli connects dragon and horse naming through categories of horse height.
claims.statement_id: Zhouli menghubungkan penamaan naga dan kuda melalui kategori tinggi kuda.
claims.quote: Longma interconnects traditional Chinese beliefs about dragons and horses. An early example comes from the Zhouli (周禮; 'Rites of Zhou'), which differentiates names for horses of different heights, measured in the chi (尺; 'Chinese foot') (historically around 23–33 centimeters, see Chinese units of measurement).

claims.statement: The Zhouli text says horses of eight chi and above are called long (龍, dragon), seven chi and above lai (騋), and six chi and above ma (馬, horse).
claims.statement_id: Teks Zhouli menyebut kuda setinggi delapan chi ke atas disebut long (龍, naga), tujuh chi ke atas disebut lai (騋), dan enam chi ke atas disebut ma (馬, kuda).
claims.quote: 廋人：掌十有二閑之政教，以阜馬、佚特、教駣、攻駒，及祭馬祖、祭閑之先牧，及執駒、散馬耳、圉馬。正校人員選。馬八尺以上為龍，七尺以上為騋，六尺以上為馬。

claims.statement: The Liji text says that when governance is in harmony, among other portents "the river brings forth the horse chart" (河出馬圖) and the tortoise and dragon (龜龍) are in the palace ponds.
claims.statement_id: Teks Liji menyebut bahwa ketika tata kelola selaras, antara lain "河出馬圖" (sungai mengeluarkan bagan kuda) terjadi, dan kura-kura serta naga (龜龍) berada di kolam istana.
claims.quote: 故天降膏露，地出醴泉，山出器車，河出馬圖 ... 皆在郊棷，龜龍在宫沼

claims.statement: An ancient commentary quoted in the article states that its shape is a horse's body with dragon scales, its height is eight ch'ih five ts'un, and a true dragon horse has wings at its sides and walks on water without sinking.
claims.statement_id: Komentar kuno yang dikutip artikel ini menyatakan bahwa bentuknya bertubuh kuda tetapi bersisik naga, tingginya delapan chi lima cun, dan longma sejati bersayap di sisinya serta berjalan di atas air tanpa tenggelam.
claims.quote: As a being its shape consists of a horse's body, yet it has dragon scales. Therefore it is called 'dragon horse'. Its height is eight ch'ih five ts'un. A true dragon horse has wings at its sides and walks upon the water without sinking.

claims.statement: The same commentary states that if a holy man is on the throne, the dragon horse comes out of the midst of the river carrying a map on its back.
claims.statement_id: Komentar yang sama menyatakan bahwa jika seorang suci berada di atas takhta, longma keluar dari tengah sungai sambil membawa peta di punggungnya.
claims.quote: If a holy man is on the throne it comes out of the midst of the Ming river, carrying a map on its back.

claims.statement: According to the article, the Hetu is traditionally linked with prehistoric Chinese rulers: a longma revealed the Hetu to Fu Xi or Shun.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ini, Hetu secara tradisional dikaitkan dengan penguasa Tiongkok prasejarah: seekor longma menyingkapkan Hetu kepada Fu Xi atau Shun.
claims.quote: They are traditionally linked with prehistoric Chinese rulers, a longma revealed the Hetu to Fu Xi or Shun

claims.statement: The 10th-century Taiping Imperial Reader is said to state that a longma that appeared in 741 was considered a good omen for Emperor Xuanzong of Tang; it was spotted blue and red, covered with scales, had a dragon-like mane, neighed like a flute, and could cover three hundred miles.
claims.statement_id: Taiping Imperial Reader (abad ke-10) disebut menyatakan bahwa seekor longma yang muncul pada 741 dianggap pertanda baik bagi Kaisar Xuanzong dari Tang; ia berbintik biru dan merah, bersisik, surainya mirip naga, ringkikannya seperti suara seruling, dan mampu menempuh tiga ratus mil.
claims.quote: The 10th-century Taiping Imperial Reader says a longma that appeared in 741 was considered as a good omen for Emperor Xuanzong of Tang. ... It was spotted blue and red, and covered with scales. Its mane resembled that of a dragon, and its neighing was like the tone of a flute. It could cover three hundred miles.

claims.statement: In the account quoted in the article, the longma's mother was a common horse that became pregnant by drinking water from the river in which it was bathed.
claims.statement_id: Dalam catatan yang dikutip artikel ini, induk longma itu adalah kuda biasa yang hamil setelah meminum air sungai tempatnya dimandikan.
claims.quote: Its mother was a common horse which had become pregnant by drinking water from a river in which it was bathed.

claims.statement: A passage quoted in the article records a story that dragons, changing form, couple with mares and the offspring is a wild horse (dragon-horse) difficult to tame and fierce in nature.
claims.statement_id: Kutipan dalam artikel ini mencatat cerita bahwa naga yang berganti wujud kawin dengan kuda betina dan keturunannya adalah kuda liar (kuda-naga) yang sulit dijinakkan dan bersifat garang.
claims.quote: The dragons, changing their form, couple with mares. The offspring is a wild species of horse (dragon-horse) difficult to tame and of a fierce nature.

claims.statement: Luanniao, or luan, is a legendary spirit bird of Chinese mythology.
claims.statement_id: Luanniao atau luan adalah burung roh legenda mitologi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: 鸞（らん）は中国神話の伝説の霊鳥。日本の江戸時代の百科事典『和漢三才図会』には、実在の鳥として記載されている。

claims.statement: The Shanhaijing locates luan in paradisiacal regions where it sings spontaneously.
claims.statement_id: Shanhaijing menempatkan luan di daerah surgawi tempat ia bernyanyi spontan.
claims.quote: Chapters 7 and 16 of the Classic of Mountains and Seas describes the luan as inhabiting paradisiacal areas where it sings spontaneously. In Chapter 11, its features are reminiscent of the fenghuang. It is said to trample on snakes while wearing one on its breast. In other sections, it is mentioned as carrying a shield.

claims.statement: The Shuowen Jiezi describes red coloring, five-colored markings, and a chicken-like body.
claims.statement_id: Shuowen Jiezi menggambarkannya merah dengan tanda lima warna dan tubuh menyerupai ayam.
claims.quote: The Shuowen Jiezi defines the bird as born from the sperm of Chìdì. It is red in colour with five-coloured markings. Its body is shaped like that of a chicken. It sings in the five standard pitches and appears when hymns of praise are sung to rulers. It also described the luan as being "the essence of divine birds".

claims.statement: The Sancai Tuhui calls this bird a transformation of a divine spirit.
claims.statement_id: Sancai Tuhui menyebut burung ini sebagai perubahan suatu roh ilahi.
claims.quote: The Sancai Tuhui states that the bird is the transformation of a divine spirit.

claims.statement: The Wakan Sansai Zue says its blood can serve as adhesive for musical-instrument strings.
claims.statement_id: Wakan Sansai Zue menyebut darahnya dapat menjadi perekat senar alat musik.
claims.quote: The Japanese Wakan Sansai Zue of the Edo period further states that due to the viscosity of the luan's blood, it could be used as an adhesive for attaching strings to musical instruments.

claims.statement: This classical text says that on Mount Nüchuang there is a bird shaped like a zhai (a long-tailed bird) with five-colored markings, named Luanniao, and when it is seen the world is at peace.
claims.statement_id: Teks klasik ini menyebut di Gunung Nüchuang ada burung berbentuk seperti zhai (sejenis burung berekor panjang) dengan corak lima warna, bernama Luanniao, dan bila terlihat maka dunia damai tenteram.
claims.quote: 曰女牀之山，其陽多赤銅，其陰多石涅〈即楚石也，楚人名為涅石，秦名為羽涅也，本草經亦名曰石涅也。〉，其獸多虎豹犀兕。有鳥焉，其狀如翟而五采文〈翟似雉而大長尾，或作𪇱。𪇱，鵰屬也。〉，名曰鸞鳥，見則天下安寧

claims.statement: Like the fenghuang, a sighting of the luan indicates an omen of peace; an early legend says the luan was presented as tribute by northwestern tribes to King Cheng of Zhou as a symbol of submission to his virtue.
claims.statement_id: Seperti fenghuang, penampakan luan menandakan pertanda damai; sebuah legenda awal menyebut luan dipersembahkan suku-suku barat laut kepada Raja Cheng dari Zhou sebagai lambang ketundukan pada kebajikannya.
claims.quote: Like the fenghuang, a sighting of the luan indicates an omen of peace. An early legend thought to be from the Warring States period states that the luan was presented as a tribute by northwestern tribes to King Cheng of Zhou as a symbol of submission to his virtue.

claims.statement: In the Classic of Mountains and Seas, the luan is described as one of the three five-coloured birds, along with the huang and feng birds; the luan would sing while the feng would dance to accompany it.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Classic of Mountains and Seas, luan digambarkan sebagai salah satu dari tiga burung lima warna bersama burung huang dan feng; luan bernyanyi sementara feng menari mengiringinya.
claims.quote: In the Classic of Mountains and Seas, the luan is described as being one of the three five-coloured birds, along with huang and feng bird. The luan would sing while the feng would dance to accompany it.

claims.statement: Qianliyan is a Chinese sea and door god guarding Mazu temples with Shunfeng'er.
claims.statement_id: Qianliyan adalah dewa laut dan pintu Tiongkok yang menjaga kuil Mazu bersama Shunfeng'er.
claims.quote: Qianliyan is a Chinese sea and door god. He usually appears with Shunfeng'er as a guardian of the temples of the sea goddess Mazu.

claims.statement: His name means thousand-li eyes and expresses far-seeing ability.
claims.statement_id: Namanya berarti mata seribu li dan melambangkan kemampuan melihat jauh.
claims.quote: The name "Qianliyan" literally means "Thousand Li Eyes" or "League Eyes" but may be taken more generally as "Hawkeye", "Lynx-Eyed", "Far-Seeing", or even "All-Seeing" or "Clairvoyant" as a distance of 1,000 li was idiomatic in Chinese for any great distance. It also appears as Qianli Yan and Qian Li Yan. His partner Shunfeng'er's name similarly means "Sharp-Eared" or "All-Hearing".

claims.statement: During the Ming period, he was also known as Li Lou.
claims.statement_id: Pada zaman Ming, ia juga dikenal sebagai Li Lou.
claims.quote: Under the Ming, Qianliyan was also known as Li Lou.

claims.statement: Journey to the West portrays him as the personified eyes of the Jade Emperor and one of his lieutenants.
claims.statement_id: Journey to the West menampilkannya sebagai personifikasi mata Kaisar Giok dan salah satu bawahannya.
claims.quote: Qianliyan is first attested in the early-16th century novel Journey to the West, where he appears as the personified form of the Taoist Jade Emperor's eyes and one of his lieutenants.

claims.statement: Journey to the South portrays him as a lieutenant of the Emperor of Flowering Brightness.
claims.statement_id: Journey to the South menampilkannya sebagai bawahan Kaisar Flowering Brightness.
claims.quote: Qianliyan next appeared as a lieutenant of the Emperor of Flowering Brightness ... in Yu Xiangdou's Journey to the South and as a character in Xu Zhonglin's Creation of the Gods.

claims.statement: In the novel's text, the Jade Emperor commands Qianliyan (千里眼) and Shunfeng'er (順風耳) to open the South Heavenly Gate and look; the two generals go out and see clearly and hear distinctly.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks novel ini, Kaisar Giok memerintahkan Qianliyan (千里眼) dan Shunfeng'er (順風耳) membuka Gerbang Langit Selatan untuk mengamati; kedua jenderal itu keluar dan "melihat dengan jelas, mendengar dengan terang".
claims.quote: 即命千里眼、順風耳開南天門觀看。二將果奉旨出門外，看的真，聽的明。

claims.statement: In the novel's text, Qianliyan and Shunfeng'er step out from the ranks of the celestial court and report that the monkey is a stone monkey born three hundred years earlier.
claims.statement_id: Dalam teks novel ini, Qianliyan dan Shunfeng'er tampil dari barisan para pejabat langit dan melaporkan bahwa monyet itu adalah monyet batu yang lahir tiga ratus tahun sebelumnya.
claims.quote: 班中閃出千里眼、順風耳道：「這猴乃三百年前天產石猴。當時不以為然，不知這幾年在何方修煉成仙，降龍伏虎，強銷死籍也。」

claims.statement: Qianliyan's sharp vision is employed to protect sailors at night and during fog and other bad weather; in some accounts he can see everything in the world.
claims.statement_id: Penglihatan tajam Qianliyan dipakai untuk melindungi pelaut pada malam hari serta saat kabut dan cuaca buruk; dalam beberapa kisah ia dapat melihat segala sesuatu di dunia.
claims.quote: Qianliyan's sharp vision is employed to help protect sailors at night and during fog and other inclement weather. In some accounts, he is capable of seeing everything in the world.

claims.statement: Qianliyan is most often portrayed as a demon defeated and tamed or befriended by the sea goddess Mazu.
claims.statement_id: Qianliyan paling sering digambarkan sebagai iblis yang dikalahkan dan dijinakkan atau dijadikan sahabat oleh dewi laut Mazu.
claims.quote: Qianliyan is most often portrayed as a demon defeated and tamed or befriended by the sea goddess Mazu.

claims.statement: By one account, he and Shunfeng'er appeared off Meizhou Island during a storm and were defeated by Mazu's magical silk scarf, which blew clouds of sand into their eyes and ears.
claims.statement_id: Menurut satu kisah, ia dan Shunfeng'er muncul di lepas Pulau Meizhou saat badai dan dikalahkan oleh selendang sutra ajaib Mazu yang meniupkan awan pasir ke mata dan telinga mereka.
claims.quote: By one account, he and Shunfeng'er appeared off Meizhou Island during a storm and were defeated by Mazu's magical silk scarf, which blew clouds of sand into their eyes and ears.

claims.statement: In one account, the pair were originally warriors or guards of Di Xin, and their powers fail when they are covered in the blood of a black dog.
claims.statement_id: Menurut satu kisah, keduanya semula prajurit atau pengawal Di Xin; kekuatan mereka lenyap ketika mereka dilumuri darah anjing hitam.
claims.quote: In still another account, the pair were originally warriors or guards of Di Xin. ... Their powers fail them when he covers them in the blood of a black dog

claims.statement: In art, Qianliyan typically appears as a green-skinned demon shielding his eyes from the sun's glare.
claims.statement_id: Dalam seni, Qianliyan biasanya tampil sebagai iblis berkulit hijau yang menaungi matanya dari silau matahari.
claims.quote: Qianliyan typically appears as a green-skinned demon shielding his eyes from the sun's glare.

claims.statement: During the annual pilgrimage from Dajia to Beigang, Mazu's idol is accompanied by figures of Qianliyan and Shunfeng'er about three metres tall, played by masked men on stilts.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ziarah tahunan dari Dajia ke Beigang, patung Mazu diiringi figur Qianliyan dan Shunfeng'er setinggi sekitar tiga meter yang diperankan pria bertopeng di atas egrang.
claims.quote: During the 8-day, 250-kilometer (155 mi) annual pilgrimages from Dajia to Beigang, Mazu's idol is accompanied by 10-foot (3 m) figures of Qianliyan and Shunfeng'er played by masked men on stilts.

claims.statement: Taowu is a Chinese mythological creature counted among the Four Perils.
claims.statement_id: Taowu adalah makhluk mitologis Tiongkok yang termasuk Empat Bahaya.
claims.quote: Taowu is a mythical creature mentioned in the Chinese classics. Along with Hundun, Qiongqi, and Taotie, it is one of the Four Perils.

claims.statement: Elements of its name are linked to a tree stump and a stool.
claims.statement_id: Unsur namanya dikaitkan dengan tunggul kayu dan bangku.
claims.quote: Taowu is composed of two characters, both of which are quite rare. Paul W. Kroll et al link 檮/梼 tao with a block of wood or a tree stump, and 杌 wu is normally used to refer to a stool. In Records of the Grand Historian, 檮 tao is written with the character 梼, which is also the simplified form.

claims.statement: Its meaning expanded from a particular beast to mythical beings and stubborn people.
claims.statement_id: Maknanya berkembang dari makhluk tertentu menjadi makhluk mitologis dan orang keras kepala.
claims.quote: Semantically, the name originally referred to some sort of beast. However, its meaning extended over time to refer to mythical creatures in general, a now-lost text referring to the history of Chu, and violent, stubborn people.

claims.statement: Sima Qian portrays it as a rebellious and destructive son of Zhuanxu.
claims.statement_id: Sima Qian menggambarkannya sebagai anak Zhuanxu yang memberontak dan merusak.
claims.quote: Sima Qian records Taowu as a label given to a rebellious, destructive son of Zhuanxu, the progenitor of the Youyu clan. He was devoid of ability, stubborn, ignorant to instruction, and could not be appeased.

claims.statement: The Guoyu and Shuo Yuan locate Taowu on Mount Pi during the Shang period.
claims.statement_id: Guoyu dan Shuo Yuan menempatkan Taowu di Gunung Pi pada zaman Shang.
claims.quote: Guoyu and Shuo Yuan record Taowu as residing at Mt. Pi (丕山) during the Shang dynasty.

claims.statement: The Shiji text says the house of Zhuanxu (顓頊氏) had an untalented son who could not be taught and did not understand speech, whom the world called Taowu (檮杌).
claims.statement_id: Teks Shiji menyebut bahwa keluarga Zhuanxu (顓頊氏) memiliki seorang putra yang tidak berbakat, tidak dapat dididik, dan tidak mengerti ucapan, yang oleh dunia disebut Taowu (檮杌).
claims.quote: 少暤氏有不才子，毀信惡忠，崇飾惡言，天下謂之窮奇。顓頊氏有不才子，不可教訓，不知話言，天下謂之檮杌。

claims.statement: The Shiji text says Taowu belongs to the "three clans" that long troubled the world, and that Shun later banished the "four villain clans" (四凶族) to the four frontiers to ward off goblins (螭魅).
claims.statement_id: Teks Shiji menyebut bahwa Taowu termasuk dalam "tiga kaum" yang lama menjadi kekhawatiran dunia, dan bahwa Shun kemudian mengasingkan "empat kaum jahat" (四凶族) ke empat penjuru perbatasan untuk menangkal siluman (螭魅).
claims.quote: 顓頊氏有不才子，不可教訓，不知話言，天下謂之檮杌。此三族世憂之。 ... 天下惡之，比之三凶。舜賓於四門，乃流四凶族，遷于四裔，以御螭魅

claims.statement: The Shenyijing text describes a beast in the western wilds that looks like a tiger but with dog fur, a human face, tiger feet, a pig's mouth and tusks and a tail one zhang eight chi long, which throws the wilds into disorder; it is named Taowu, also called Aohen and Nanxun.
claims.statement_id: Teks Shenyijing menggambarkan binatang di wilayah liar barat yang mirip harimau tetapi berbulu anjing, berwajah manusia, berkaki harimau, bermulut dan bertaring babi, berekor satu zhang delapan chi, dan mengacau wilayah itu; namanya Taowu, juga disebut Aohen dan Nanxun.
claims.quote: 西方荒中有獸焉，其狀如虎而犬毛，長二尺，人面虎足，猪口牙，尾長一丈八尺，攪乱荒中，名梼杌，一名傲狠，一名難訓。

claims.statement: According to the article, the trouble he caused continued through Emperor Yao's reign until Emperor Shun received him with the other Four Perils, banishing them to the outer reaches of the kingdom and expelling evil spirits.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ini, kekacauan yang ditimbulkannya berlanjut sepanjang masa Kaisar Yao hingga Kaisar Shun menerimanya bersama Empat Bahaya lain, mengasingkan mereka ke pelosok kerajaan, dan mengusir roh jahat.
claims.quote: The trouble he caused would continue throughout the reign of Emperor Yao of the Taotang clan, until Emperor Shun of the Youyu clan would receive him along with the other Four Perils, banishing them to the outer reaches of the kingdom and expelling evil spirits.

claims.statement: According to the article, the Book of Gods and Strange Things records Taowu as a monster with a human face, tiger feet, a pig's mouth and teeth and an 18-foot tail.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ini, Book of Gods and Strange Things mencatat Taowu sebagai monster berwajah manusia, berkaki harimau, bermulut dan bergigi babi, dan berekor 18 kaki.
claims.quote: The Book of Gods and Strange Things records Taowu as a monster with a human face, a tiger's feet, a pig's mouth and teeth, and a tail 18 feet long.

claims.statement: Yaoguai are a diverse category of supernaturally powered beings in Chinese folklore.
claims.statement_id: Yaoguai adalah kategori beragam makhluk berkekuatan gaib dalam cerita rakyat Tiongkok.
claims.quote: Yaoguai (Chinese: 妖怪; pinyin: yāoguài) represent a broad and diverse class of ambiguous creatures in Chinese folklore and mythology defined by the possession of supernatural powers and by having attributes that partake of the quality of the weird, the strange or the unnatural. They are especially associated with transformation and enchantment.

claims.statement: The category is associated with transformation and enchantment.
claims.statement_id: Kategori ini dikaitkan dengan perubahan wujud dan pesona gaib.
claims.quote: Yaoguai (Chinese: 妖怪; pinyin: yāoguài) represent a broad and diverse class of ambiguous creatures in Chinese folklore and mythology defined by the possession of supernatural powers and by having attributes that partake of the quality of the weird, the strange or the unnatural. They are especially associated with transformation and enchantment.

claims.statement: Abilities vary by being and may include illusions, hypnosis, or causing disease.
claims.statement_id: Kemampuan berbeda menurut makhluknya dan dapat mencakup ilusi, hipnosis, atau menyebabkan penyakit.
claims.quote: Yaoguai vary considerably from one another in appearance and powers, and depending on the particular individual or type, as being capable of shapeshifting, creating illusions, hypnosis, controlling minds, causing disease, clairvoyance, and draining the life force of mortals.

claims.statement: Tales generally regard yaoguai as dangerous and capable of harmful influence on people.
claims.statement_id: Kisah umumnya menganggap yaoguai berbahaya dan dapat membawa pengaruh buruk kepada manusia.
claims.quote: While yaoguai are not evil in the sense Western demons are, they are usually weird and dangerous, tending to exert a baleful influence on mankind.

claims.statement: According to the article, yaoguai often dwell in remote areas or on the fringes of civilization where they produce all manner of unexplainable phenomena and mischief, and they often have predatory or malevolent tendencies.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ini, yaoguai sering tinggal di daerah terpencil atau di tepi peradaban, tempat mereka menimbulkan berbagai gejala yang tak terjelaskan dan kekacauan; mereka sering memiliki kecenderungan memangsa atau berniat jahat.
claims.quote: They often dwell in remote areas or on the fringes of civilization where they produce all manner of unexplainable phenomena and mischief. They often have predatory or malevolent tendencies.

claims.statement: Possession of supernatural power defines the yaoguai and distinguishes them from other monsters; typical powers ascribed to them include shapeshifting, creating illusions, mind control, clairvoyance, possession of human beings, and control over natural forces.
claims.statement_id: Kepemilikan kekuatan gaib mendefinisikan yaoguai dan membedakannya dari monster lain; kekuatan yang lazim dikaitkan dengannya meliputi perubahan wujud, penciptaan ilusi, kendali pikiran, kewaskitaan, perasukan manusia, dan kendali atas kekuatan alam.
claims.quote: Possession of supernatural power defines the yaoguai, distinguishing them from other monsters. Descriptions of the abilities of these beings vary considerably. Typical powers ascribed to them include shapeshifting, the manufacture of illusions, mind control, clairvoyance, the possession of human beings, and the control over natural forces.

claims.statement: The article gives examples: Baigujing, a "white skeleton essence", is described as an adept shapeshifter taking on the forms of several people to deceive her opponents, while Bai Suzhen, a white snake fairy, unleashes a supernatural flood against a temple.
claims.statement_id: Artikel ini memberi contoh: Baigujing, "esensi kerangka putih", digambarkan piawai berubah wujud menjadi banyak orang untuk menipu lawannya, sedangkan Bai Suzhen, peri ular putih, melepaskan banjir gaib terhadap sebuah kuil.
claims.quote: Baigujing, a white skeleton essence, is described as an adept shapeshifter, taking on the forms of multiple people in an attempt to deceive her opponents. Others are capable of control over elemental forces, as when Bai Suzhen, a white snake fairy unleashes a supernatural flood against a temple.

claims.statement: According to the article, the classic text Zuo Zhuan states that when people abandon constancy, this causes the yao to emerge.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ini, teks klasik Zuo Zhuan menyatakan bahwa ketika orang meninggalkan kebajikan yang tetap, hal itu membuat yao bermunculan.
claims.quote: According to the classic text Zuo Zhuan, "when people abandon constancy then this causes the yao to emerge"

claims.statement: According to the article, in more superstitious times confusion, strange and unexplainable disease, eerie sights and sounds, and unexplained murders and missing persons were attributed to yaoguai.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ini, pada masa yang lebih percaya takhayul, kebingungan, penyakit aneh yang tak terjelaskan, pemandangan seram, bunyi aneh, serta pembunuhan dan orang hilang yang tak terjelaskan dianggap ulah yaoguai.
claims.quote: In more superstitious times, confusion and bewilderment, strange and unexplainable disease, eerie sights and strange sounds, and cases of unexplained murders and missing persons were attributed to them

claims.statement: According to Wiktionary, the Chinese concept 妖怪 (yāoguài) does not map directly to any specific English term and is often translated as "monster" or "demon".
claims.statement_id: Menurut Wiktionary, konsep 妖怪 (yāoguài) tidak memiliki padanan langsung dalam satu istilah Inggris dan sering diterjemahkan sebagai "monster" atau "iblis".
claims.quote: The Chinese concept of 妖怪 (yāoguài) does not map directly to any specific English term and it's often translated as “monster” or “demon”.

claims.statement: Wiktionary defines 妖怪 (usually in Chinese mythology) as a supernatural being, monster, demon, strange apparition or spirit.
claims.statement_id: Wiktionary mendefinisikan 妖怪 (biasanya dalam mitologi Tiongkok) sebagai makhluk gaib, monster, iblis, penampakan aneh, atau roh.
claims.quote: 妖怪 (usually in Chinese mythology) supernatural being; monster; demon; strange apparition; spirit;

claims.statement: Wiktionary cites a sentence from the Book of Han (Ban Gu, volume 89, 111 CE): after a long time there were frequent apparitions (妖怪) in the palace; the king asked Sui about it, and Sui believed great sorrow would follow.
claims.statement_id: Wiktionary mengutip contoh kalimat dari Book of Han (Ban Gu, volume 89, 111 M): setelah beberapa waktu, di istana sering terdapat penampakan aneh (妖怪); sang raja menanyakannya kepada Sui, yang mengira akan ada kesedihan besar.
claims.quote: 111 CE, Ban Gu, Book of Han (volume 89) 久之，宮中數有妖怪，王以問遂，遂以為有大憂，宮室將空。

claims.statement: Yu Shi is a Chinese rain deity also linked to Chisongzi.
claims.statement_id: Yu Shi adalah dewa hujan Tiongkok yang juga dihubungkan dengan Chisongzi.
claims.quote: Yu Shi (traditional Chinese: 雨師; simplified Chinese: 雨师; pinyin: Yǔ Shī; lit. 'Master of Rain') is a Chinese spirit or god of rain, also known as or conflated with Red Pine (Chisong, 赤松, or Chisongzi – Master Red Pine), among other names. Translations of Yu Shi into English include "Lord of Rain" and "Leader of Rain".

claims.statement: He often appears with the wind deity Feng Bo and thunder deity Lei Gong.
claims.statement_id: Ia kerap tampil bersama Feng Bo, dewa angin, dan Lei Gong, dewa guntur.
claims.quote: Yu Shi in Chinese folk religion and Chinese mythology generally appears in association with Feng Bo, the god of the wind; and Lei Gong, the god of thunder. There are both current religious activities and historical mythical stories associated with Yu Shi. Various references in poetry and popular culture also exist, for example in the Chu ci poems "Tian Wen" and "Yuan You".

claims.statement: One version says Chisongzi ends a drought by sprinkling water from a bowl.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah versi mengatakan Chisongzi mengakhiri kekeringan dengan memercikkan air dari mangkuk.
claims.quote: According to certain versions, a certain Chisongzi (Chinese: 赤松子; pinyin: Chì-Sōng-Zǐ; Wade–Giles: Ch'ih-sung-tzu; lit. 'Master Red Pine') during the reign of Shennong ended a severe drought by sprinkling water from an earthen bowl and was rewarded by being made the Lord of Rain with a dwelling on the mythical Kunlun Mountain.

claims.statement: Another portrayal gives him the form of a silkworm chrysalis.
claims.statement_id: Penggambaran lain memberikan bentuk kepompong ulat sutra.
claims.quote: In another form, Chi Songzi is depicted as a chrysalis of a silkworm who has a concubine whose face is black, holds a snake in each hand, and has a red snake coming out of one ear and a green snake coming out of the other.

claims.statement: Yu Shi assists Chiyou at Zhuolu before defeat by the drought goddess Ba.
claims.statement_id: Yu Shi membantu Chiyou pada pertempuran Zhuolu, lalu dikalahkan dewi kekeringan Ba.
claims.quote: Yu Shi (together with Feng Bo) is said to have aided Chiyou in his struggle against the Yellow Emperor during the Battle of Zhuolu, but was defeated by the intervention of the drought goddess Ba.

claims.statement: The Shanhaijing text mentions the country of Yushiqie (雨師妾), whose people are dark-skinned, hold a snake in each hand, and have a green snake at the left ear and a red snake at the right ear.
claims.statement_id: Teks Shanhaijing menyebut negeri Yushiqie (雨師妾), yang penduduknya berkulit gelap, memegang seekor ular di tiap tangan, dengan ular hijau di telinga kiri dan ular merah di telinga kanan.
claims.quote: 雨師妾國一作「雨師妾」在其北，其為人黑，兩手各操一蛇，左耳有青蛇，右耳有赤蛇。

claims.statement: The Zhouli text says burning offerings (槱燎) are used to worship Sizhong, Siming, Fengshi (Master of Wind) and Yushi (雨師, Master of Rain).
claims.statement_id: Teks Zhouli menyebut bahwa pembakaran persembahan (槱燎) dipakai untuk memuja Sizhong, Siming, Fengshi (Guru Angin), dan Yushi (雨師, Guru Hujan).
claims.quote: 以禋祀祀昊天上帝，以實柴祀日月星辰，以槱燎祀司中、司命、風師、雨師。

claims.statement: The Shanhaijing text says Chiyou attacked the Yellow Emperor, Yinglong held back water, and Chiyou then summoned Fengbo and Yushi (風伯雨師), who unleashed a great wind and rain.
claims.statement_id: Teks Shanhaijing menyebut bahwa Chiyou menyerang Kaisar Kuning, Yinglong menahan air, lalu Chiyou memanggil Fengbo dan Yushi (風伯雨師) yang melepaskan angin dan hujan besar.
claims.quote: 蚩尤作兵伐黄帝，黄帝乃令應龍攻之冀州之野。應龍畜水。蚩尤請風伯雨師，縱大風雨。

claims.statement: The Yuanyou poem in the Chuci places Yushi (雨師) at the left as an attendant and Leigong (雷公) at the right as a guard.
claims.statement_id: Puisi Yuanyou dalam Chuci menyebut Yushi (雨師) di sisi kiri sebagai pengiring dan Leigong (雷公) di sisi kanan sebagai pengawal.
claims.quote: 後文昌使掌行兮，選署衆神以並轂。路曼曼其脩遠兮，徐弭節而高厲。左雨師使徑侍兮，右雷公以爲衛。

claims.statement: According to the article, Yu Shi is worshiped by Han Chinese, Maonan people and others in modern southwest China as an important rain god, with ritual prayer ceremonies to entreat for rain.
claims.statement_id: Menurut artikel ini, Yu Shi dipuja oleh orang Han, suku Maonan, dan lainnya di Tiongkok barat daya masa kini sebagai dewa hujan penting, dengan upacara doa untuk memohon hujan.
claims.quote: Yu Shi is worshiped by Han Chinese, Maonan people, and other people in modern southwest China as an important rain god with ritual prayer ceremonies performed to entreat for rain.

claims.statement: Zhulong is a giant red dragon and solar deity in Chinese mythology.
claims.statement_id: Zhulong adalah naga merah raksasa dan dewa matahari dalam mitologi Tiongkok.
claims.quote: Zhulong /ˈdʒuːlɒŋ/ or Zhuyin /ˈdʒuːjɪn/, also known in English as the Torch Dragon, was a giant red solar dragon and god in Chinese mythology. It supposedly had a human's face and snake's body, created day and night by opening and closing its eyes, and created seasonal winds by breathing.

claims.statement: He is portrayed with a human face and a serpent's body.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan berwajah manusia dan bertubuh ular.
claims.quote: Zhulong /ˈdʒuːlɒŋ/ or Zhuyin /ˈdʒuːjɪn/, also known in English as the Torch Dragon, was a giant red solar dragon and god in Chinese mythology. It supposedly had a human's face and snake's body, created day and night by opening and closing its eyes, and created seasonal winds by breathing.

claims.statement: Opening and closing his eyes produces day and night, while breathing produces seasonal winds.
claims.statement_id: Membuka dan menutup matanya menciptakan siang dan malam, sedangkan napasnya menciptakan angin musim.
claims.quote: Zhulong /ˈdʒuːlɒŋ/ or Zhuyin /ˈdʒuːjɪn/, also known in English as the Torch Dragon, was a giant red solar dragon and god in Chinese mythology. It supposedly had a human's face and snake's body, created day and night by opening and closing its eyes, and created seasonal winds by breathing.

claims.statement: The Chu Ci contains name variants Chuolong and Zhuolong.
claims.statement_id: Chu Ci memuat varian nama Chuolong dan Zhuolong.
claims.quote: In the Chu Ci, Zhulong is also rendered as Chuolong, which can variously mean "Distant" or "Quarrelsome Dragon", and as Zhuolong, variously "Outstanding" or "Departed Dragon". According to present reconstructions, these variant characters 逴 (now chuò) and 趠 (now zhuó) sounded closer to the pronunciation of 燭 in old Chinese, although not homophonous.

claims.statement: The names Zhuyin and Zhulong occur in Han-period classical texts.
claims.statement_id: Nama Zhuyin dan Zhulong ditemukan dalam teks klasik zaman Han.
claims.quote: The names "Zhuyin" and "Zhulong" appear in classic Chinese texts from the Han (3rd century BCE – 3rd century CE) that record the myths of the Zhou (12th–3rd century BCE).

claims.statement: The Shanhaijing gives parallel accounts of Zhuyin and Zhulong.
claims.statement_id: Shanhaijing memberikan kisah sejajar mengenai Zhuyin dan Zhulong.
claims.quote: The Classic of Mountains and Seas (c. 3rd century BCE - 1st century CE) records parallel myths about Zhuyin and Zhulong.

claims.statement: The Shanhaijing text names the god of Mount Zhong (鍾山) as Zhuyin (燭陰): when he looks it is day, when he closes his eyes it is night, his blowing makes winter and his exhaling makes summer; he does not drink, eat or breathe (rest), his breath becomes wind, and his body is a thousand li long.
claims.statement_id: Teks Shanhaijing menyebut dewa Gunung Zhong (鍾山) bernama Zhuyin (燭陰): ketika ia melihat jadilah siang, ketika memejam jadilah malam, tiupannya menjadi musim dingin dan embusannya musim panas; ia tidak minum, makan, atau bernapas (beristirahat), napasnya menjadi angin, dan panjang tubuhnya seribu li.
claims.quote: 鍾山之神名曰燭陰，視為晝，瞑為夜，吹為冬，呼為夏，不飲，不食，不息，息為風，身長千里。

claims.statement: The same text describes the god of Mount Zhong named Zhuyin (燭陰) as having a human face and a snake body, red in colour, and dwelling at the foot of Mount Zhong.

claims.statement_id: Erya menjelaskan shen sebagai kerang yao yang besar.
claims.quote: The word used to mean a shellfish, or mollusk, identified as an oyster, mussel, or giant clam such as the Pearl of Lao Tzu. While early Chinese dictionaries treat shèn as a general term for "mollusca", the Erya defines it as a large yáo (珧) "shellfish", "clam", "scallop", or "nacre".

claims.statement: Eberhard notes uncertainty about why those shellfish were placed in tombs.
claims.statement_id: Eberhard mencatat ketidakpastian alasan kerang itu ditempatkan dalam makam.
